C0.quote: sequential voting (as in roll call votes) is theoretically preferable to simultaneous voting
C0.note: Strategic and experimental analysis of simultaneous vs sequential voting procedures with outside pressure.

C1.quote: Experimental results, however, show severe deviations from the equilibrium strategy in sequential voting
C1.note: Equilibrium analysis (Props 1-3, mostly from prior work) plus a lab experiment with regression; experiments take most of the paper.

C2.1.quote: players have two possible actions, called “Yes” and “No.”

C2.2.quote: players have two possible actions, called “Yes” and “No.”
C2.2.note: Binary Yes/No vote on a single proposal; none of the listed formats fits.

C2.3.quote: We define the true preference of N + as voting Yes
C2.3.note: True preferences, costs and benefits are held attitudes.

C2.4.quote: “true preferences” are simply defined under the assumption that the own vote is decisive
C2.4.note: Votes are separate from true preferences, and voting against true preferences is possible.

C3.1.quote: Under complete information, sequential voting has a unique subgame perfect equilibrium
C3.1.note: Equilibrium analysis involves strategic voting; experimental voters choose freely.

C4.1.quote: with ci , Gi , and Ri as cardinal utilities
C4.1.note: Input is a binary Yes/No vote (OTH), none of RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH or PAIR, so the applicability condition fails.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: true majority results were generated 11-12 percentage points more often
C5.1.note: Rules are evaluated by true majority results, which is representation of voters' true preferences. Efficiency is also discussed (Sect. 4.3).

C5.2.quote: the result is the same as if all voters had voted according to their true preferences
C5.2.note: True majority is defined on held true preferences, separate from votes.

VOT.quote_info: Every player decided under complete information
VOT.note: Strategic equilibrium players in the theory; static true-preference, heuristic and emotional behavior is considered in the experimental analysis.

ORG.note: Outside pressure is represented only as voters' costs, not as an agent.

C7.1.note: Only one agent type (voters) is present.

C8.1.quote: Sequential voting has a unique subgame perfect equilibrium
C8.1.note: Mixed and pure Nash equilibria in simultaneous voting; SPE in sequential voting; bounded rationality discussed for deviations.

C8.2.quote: The sequential voting game has a unique subgame perfect equilibrium

claims.quote: sequential voting (as in roll call votes) is theoretically preferable to simultaneous voting
The clear theoretical superiority of sequential over simultaneous voting is not confirmed
be aware of structural differences but do not base your evaluations exclusively on theory

C9.1.note: Claims about which procedure is preferable and about real roll-call institutions.

C9.2.quote: Every player decided under complete information
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions are stated: true preferences defined via costs and benefits, strategic voters, complete information, and the experimental design. The claims are about true majorities, defined on held preferences.

C10.1.note: The paper does not state a procedural-only reading.
